definition: Declarative memory is memory for learned information that can be tested through recognition of verbal and nonverbal material after it is encoded. It includes retaining that information over time and consolidating it between learning and later recall or recognition.

reasons: The packet does not provide a general definition of declarative memory (e.g., “memory for learned information”); it only describes an experiment using “verbal and nonverbal declarative memory.”

The definition’s claim that it “can be tested through recognition of verbal and nonverbal material after it is encoded” is only partially supported: the packet says recognition memory was tested 10 minutes and one day after encoding, but it does not explicitly define declarative memory in those terms.

The definition’s references to “retaining that information over time” and “consolidating it between learning and later recall or recognition” are only indirectly supported (the packet reports overnight changes and suggests “declarative memory consolidation”), but the packet does not make these as explicit defining characteristics of declarative memory.
The sentence about “later recall or recognition” is not supported: the packet mentions recognition testing but does not discuss recall.
